bills.title: Arizona GenAI Provenance Data Requirements
bills.summary: Would require providers of generative AI systems in Arizona to embed tamper-resistant provenance data in AI-generated content.

bills.title: California Automated Decision Systems in Employment
bills.summary: Would establish comprehensive regulations for the use of automated decision systems in employment, requiring human oversight, transparency, worker data access, and anti-retaliation protections.

bills.title: California AI Displacement Worker Protections
bills.summary: Would require employers to provide advance notice and protections for workers affected by technological displacement due to AI or automation.

bills.title: Hawaii Healthcare AI Disclosure and Oversight
bills.summary: Regulates AI disclosure and oversight requirements for healthcare applications in Hawaii. Reported out of committee.

bills.title: Hawaii Companion AI Youth Data Protections
bills.summary: Companion AI and chatbot data protection bill for minors. Passed through committee.

bills.title: Hawaii Chatbot Non-Human Disclosure and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require chatbot providers to disclose to the user that they are not conversing with a human, with increased frequency for minors. Providers would be prohibited from using reward systems designed to increase engagement for minors.

bills.title: Hawaii ADMT System Transparency and Consumer Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require developers of ADMT systems to give deployers disclosures on risks and intended uses. Deployers would then be required to give disclosures to consumers about the use of such systems and of their right to access and correct the data used.

bills.title: Hawaii SNAP Food Surveillance Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit retailers from using surveillance pricing in the sale of food that is sold, or qualifies to be sold, as part of the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Sets several exemptions, such as for disclosed discounts and loyalty programs.

bills.title: Illinois Hospital AI Healthcare Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit all hospitals from using artificial intelligence to set or influence health care pricing or billing.

bills.title: Illinois Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require disclosures by entities that use personalized algorithmic pricing stating that 'this price was set by an algorithm using your personal data.'

bills.title: Illinois AI Medication Prescription Human Control Requirement
bills.summary: Would prohibit licensed medical professionals from allowing AI to prescribe medication unless the professional maintains full control and responsibility over the prescription. Would also grant rulemaking responsibilities to develop regulations for AI use in this context.

bills.title: Illinois Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety (HB 4705)
bills.summary: Would combine California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety and chatbot-related requirements.

bills.title: Illinois Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety (SB 3261)
bills.summary: Would combine California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety and chatbot-related requirements.

bills.title: Illinois AI Consumer Interaction Disclosure Mandate
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of AI to interact with consumers without disclosure that the AI system is not human. Would also mandate that consumers must be offered the ability to communicate with humans during business hours when AI is used in consumer communications.

bills.title: Illinois GenAI Content Provenance Data Requirements
bills.summary: Would require GenAI tool providers to apply provenance data to wholly-generated synthetic content. Sets other requirements for large online platforms, such as retaining provenance data in content posted on the platform.

bills.title: Illinois Companion AI Safety and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would establish comprehensive safeguards, transparency, and liability measures for companion AI products and includes special protections for minors.

bills.title: Illinois Machine-Readable Provenance Labels for Digital Content
bills.summary: Would require AI providers, large online platforms, and device manufacturers to embed and preserve machine-readable provenance labels in digital content and provide free verification tools.

bills.title: Illinois Frontier Model Safety and Reporting Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish comprehensive safety, transparency, and reporting requirements for frontier model developers. Would also mandate risk management and public accountability measures.

bills.title: Illinois AI in Nursing Practice Regulations
bills.summary: Would establish strict regulations for the use of AI in the nursing practice, ensuring human oversight, patient consent, transparency, and accountability.

bills.title: Illinois Frontier Model Transparency and Risk Management
bills.summary: Would establish robust transparency, risk management, and reporting requirements for frontier model developers and would amend state law to protect sensitive AI safety information.

bills.title: Illinois AI Training Data Consent Requirement
bills.summary: Would prohibit developers from training AI on a user's data and retaining that data indefinitely unless they provide written notice to the user and obtain the user's express written consent.

bills.title: Iowa Companion and Therapeutic Chatbot Safety Requirements
bills.summary: Would set requirements for deployers of both companion and therapeutic chatbots, including limiting user data collection, requiring age verification for minors, and requiring disclosures.

bills.title: Iowa Chatbot Safety and Minor Mental Health Access Limits
bills.summary: Would set safety, privacy, and age verification requirements for chatbot deployers, including limits on minors' access to chatbots designed for mental health counseling.
sponsors: House Committee on Economic Growth and Technology

bills.title: Kansas Resolution Opposing Federal AI Preemption
bills.summary: Nonbinding resolution expressing opposition to any future efforts to impose a moratorium on state AI policymaking or preempt state AI laws.

bills.title: Kansas Prohibition on AI Training for Harmful Purposes
bills.summary: Would prohibit the training of AI that encourages suicide, simulates human relationships, or acts as a healthcare professional.
sponsors: Committee on Federal and State Affairs

bills.title: Kansas Companion AI Chatbot Age Verification
bills.summary: Would require age verification, parental controls, and user notifications for companion AI chatbots.
sponsors: House Committee on K-12 Education Budget

bills.title: Maryland AI Behavioral Health Provider Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit AI developers from claiming that AI is a behavioral health provider and sets general disclosure requirements for AI systems.

bills.title: Maryland AI Product Liability Standards
bills.summary: Would introduce a new liability standard that holds developers and deployers accountable for harm caused by defective or dangerous AI products, and includes special provisions for risk mitigation and protection of minors.

bills.title: Missouri AI Malpractice Liability for Healthcare
bills.summary: Would amend the law to include negligent use or reliance on artificial intelligence by health care providers as grounds for malpractice liability.

bills.title: New Jersey News Platform GenAI Content Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require news platforms to clearly disclose when gen AI is used to produce news content.

bills.title: New Jersey AI Child Sexual Abuse Material Criminalization
bills.summary: Would make it a crime to offer, sell, or distribute AI or automated interactive computer technology capable of performing or simulating sexual conduct directed at children.

bills.title: New Jersey AI Relationship Simulation Restriction
bills.summary: Would prohibit providers from developing, marketing, or making available any AI relationship simulation unless it is exclusively for legitimate medical purposes, such as clinical or therapeutic treatment under the supervision of a licensed healthcare professional.

bills.title: New Jersey AI Mental Health Professional Impersonation Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit advertising AI systems as licensed mental health professionals.

bills.title: New York AI-Generated Disaster Media Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require disclosure of AI-generated or materially altered media depicting major human disasters when publicly distributed in New York. Would mandate online platforms support such labeling, including providing spoken disclosures for auditory content.

bills.title: New York Delivery Worker Algorithmic Safety and Transparency
bills.summary: Would prohibit platforms from using algorithms that require or incentivize delivery workers to meet rigid delivery times that cannot be achieved while complying with traffic and safety laws. Would also ban algorithmic practices that penalize workers for delays caused by external factors and prohibit reductions in pay for refusing to engage in unsafe or unlawful conduct. Would require platforms to disclose how algorithms affect work and grant workers the right to request written explanations for suspensions.

bills.title: Ohio Algorithmic Pricing Prohibition and Disclosure
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use or distribution of pricing algorithms that are trained with nonpublic competitor data. Would also set disclosure requirements for large entities (annual revenues > $5 million) using a pricing algorithm.

bills.title: Oregon AI Companion Self-Harm Safety Protocols
bills.summary: Would require AI companion and platform operators to clearly disclose AI interactions and implement protocols to detect and prevent harm related to suicidal ideation or self-harm, with heightened protections for minors.
sponsors: Senate Committee on Early Childhood and Behavioral Health

bills.title: Pennsylvania Chatbot Consumer Data and Advertising Restrictions
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbot suppliers from selling or sharing consumer information with a third party, as well as advertising products to users without disclosure. Would also require chatbot suppliers to maintain a written policy, which includes disclosure requirements.

bills.title: Pennsylvania Companion Chatbot Minor Access Regulation
bills.summary: Regulates the use of companion chatbots by users, including minors. Passed through committee.

bills.title: Rhode Island AI Companion Non-Human Disclosure Every 3 Hours
bills.summary: Would require operators of AI companion systems to implement safety protocols and notify users of the system's non-human status every 3 hours.

bills.title: Rhode Island AI Mental Health Professional Impersonation Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit advertising AI systems as licensed mental health professionals, modeled on Illinois HB 1806.

bills.title: South Dakota Chatbot Commercial Transaction Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require that consumers be notified when they are interacting with a chatbot during commercial transactions, modeled on Alabama HB 325.

bills.title: South Dakota Chatbot Age Verification and Minor Access Restrictions
bills.summary: Would require chatbot providers to implement age verification, restrict minor access to chatbots with human-like features, and limit minor use of therapy chatbots.

bills.title: Utah AI Regulatory Sandbox and Mitigation Agreements
bills.summary: AI regulatory sandbox bill establishing mitigation agreements for regulated AI systems. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Utah Expanding Healthcare Practitioners' AI Use
bills.summary: Health AI bill regulating AI use by healthcare practitioners. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Utah Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety
bills.summary: Frontier model catastrophic risk and chatbot child safety regulation bill. Already passed committee in prior session.

bills.title: Utah Comprehensive AI Companion Chatbot Safety Framework
bills.summary: Would establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for AI companion chatbots, with a particular focus on protecting minors and addressing risks related to emotional dependency, self-harm, and harmful content. Would require providers to implement safety protocols, conduct ongoing assessments, enable independent evaluations, and publish regular public reports on safety measures. Sets restrictions on harmful content and data sharing, mandatory disclosures that chatbots are not human, and clear account and data deletion options.

bills.title: Utah ADMT Data Privacy Framework Update
bills.summary: Would update Utah's data privacy laws by introducing new definitions for automated decision making and profiling, including requiring the development of a data privacy framework that incorporates best practices for automated decision making.

bills.title: Vermont GenAI Detection Tools and Watermarking
bills.summary: Requires providers of generative AI systems to offer tools detecting AI generated content and to give users the option to watermark AI generated content.

bills.title: Vermont AI Consumer Interaction Disclosure on Request
bills.summary: Mandates that any person or entity using generative AI to interact with consumers must clearly disclose, upon request, that the consumer is interacting with AI and not a human. If the interaction is high-risk, involving sensitive data or significant advice, the disclosure must be made prominently at the start of the interaction.

bills.title: Vermont AI Mental Health Professional Impersonation Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit advertising AI systems as licensed mental health professionals, modeled on Illinois HB 1806.

bills.title: Vermont AI Patient Communication Disclaimer and Neurological Rights
bills.summary: Mandates that patient communication generated by AI must include a disclaimer and instructions for contacting a human provider, restricts advertising and data collection for mental health chatbots, and enumerates a list of 'neurological rights.'

bills.title: Vermont AI Liability Accountability Standards
bills.summary: Prohibits claiming in court that harm was autonomously caused by artificial intelligence as a defense in civil lawsuits, placing accountability on those who develop, modify, or use AI systems.

bills.title: Virginia Independent AI Verification Organizations (Senate)
bills.summary: Companion bill to HB 797, creating frameworks for independent verification organizations (IVOs) to audit AI systems. Passed through committee.

bills.title: Virginia Independent AI Verification Organizations (House)
bills.summary: Companion bill to SB 384, creating frameworks for independent verification organizations (IVOs) to audit AI systems. Passed through committee.

bills.title: Washington AI Transparency Act (California-style)
bills.summary: GenAI transparency bill, passed out of committee. Previously incorporated a SB 53-style definition for 'covered provider.'

bills.title: Washington High-Risk AI Systems Requirements (CAIA-style)
bills.summary: High risk AI and ADMT regulation bill. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Washington Generative AI Training Data Transparency
bills.summary: GenAI training data transparency bill. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Washington AI Employment Regulation
bills.summary: AI employment regulation bill. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Washington Data-Driven Pricing Regulation
bills.summary: Data-driven pricing regulation bill. Previously passed committee.

bills.title: Washington ADMT High-Risk AI Regulation
bills.summary: ADMT and high-risk AI regulation bill. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: West Virginia AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Would prohibit advertising AI systems as licensed mental health professionals, modeled on Illinois HB 1806. Passed out of committee.

bills.title: Wisconsin Companion Chatbot Minor Access Restrictions
bills.summary: A California AB 1064-style bill (vetoed) restricting minor access to companion chatbots across a variety of use cases.

bills.title: Wisconsin AI Legal Personhood Clarification
bills.summary: Would clarify that AI is not a person and would provide statutory definitions for terms like developer, entity, and owner, in Wisconsin.

bills.title: Alabama Comprehensive Privacy Act (Connecticut-style)
bills.summary: Comprehensive privacy bill modeled on Connecticut's law, introduced by Rep. Shaw (R). Includes expanded authority for authorized agents and a unique AI model exemption for models that do not contain or expose personally identifiable data.

bills.title: Alabama App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act (ASAA) bill passed by the Alabama Senate with amendments on February 5, 2026. The bill returned to the House to consider the Senate's amendments.
bills.status_detail: Passed by the Senate with amendments on February 5, 2026. Bill goes back to the House to consider Senate's amendments.

bills.title: Arizona Comprehensive Privacy Act (Virginia-style)
bills.summary: Virginia-style comprehensive privacy bill introduced by Sen. Kuby (D). Includes the broader definition of sale (including exchanges for 'other valuable consideration'). Defines 'child' as someone under the age of 16, extending many child-specific protections to teenagers.

bills.title: Arizona Data Broker Registry and Security Requirements
bills.summary: Would require data brokers to post a public privacy notice, register annually with the state, and maintain a comprehensive information security plan.

bills.title: California Senate Privacy and Digital Technologies Committee Resolution
bills.summary: Senate resolution creating a new committee — the Senate Committee on Privacy, Digital Technologies, and Consumer Protection — with jurisdiction over bills concerning data privacy, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, consumer protection, and the California Privacy Protection Agency. Sen. Cabaldon confirmed he will chair the new committee.

bills.title: Colorado Homeowner's Insurance Financial Privacy Bill
bills.summary: Financial privacy bill regulating the processing of personal data by 'licensees' in homeowner's insurance transactions. Includes consumer rights of access, correction, deletion, and opt-in for targeted advertising and data sales. Includes data minimization, opt-in consent requirements, data protection assessments, and a private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Introduced; includes a private right of action

bills.title: Connecticut Attorney General Privacy Enforcement Funding
bills.summary: Proposal to appropriate additional money to the Connecticut office of the Attorney General for 'enforcing the state's laws concerning consumer privacy.'

bills.title: Hawaii Geolocation and Browser Data Sale Consent Requirement
bills.summary: Would require consent for the sale of geolocation information and internet browser information. Defines 'precise location' as locating a user within a geographic area of one mile radius or less. Would also ban the sale of data collected through eavesdropping or via background device microphone access.

bills.title: Illinois Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: Age-Appropriate Design Code (AADC) introduced by Sen. Rezin, modeled on the Maryland AADC. If enacted, would have an immediate effective date.

bills.title: Illinois Comprehensive Privacy Act (Virginia-style)
bills.summary: Comprehensive privacy bill introduced by Sen. Rezin (R), largely Virginia-style. Includes broader definition of 'biometric data' (including data generated from photos, video, and audio if generated to identify an individual), a narrow definition of 'sale' (monetary consideration only), and exempts pseudonymous data from consumer rights.

bills.title: Illinois BIPA Security Purpose Amendment
bills.summary: Proposed amendment to BIPA (Biometric Information Privacy Act) that would: exempt information converted to a mathematical representation that cannot recreate a biometric identifier; exempt information not reasonably usable to identify an individual; exempt biometric time clocks; allow biometric identifiers for security purposes; add a cure requirement to the private right of action; and add an exemption for entities whose employees are covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

bills.title: Illinois Data Broker Delete Act
bills.summary: Delete Act-style bill that would require data brokers to register with the state annually and would require the state to establish an accessible deletion mechanism allowing consumers to submit one deletion request to all registered data brokers.

bills.title: Iowa App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act (ASAA) framework bill introduced by Sen. Alons (R) on February 4, aligning with the models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025.

bills.title: Maryland MODPA Enforcement Division and Privacy Working Group
bills.summary: Would create a 'Division of Data Protection' within the Maryland AG's office to enforce MODPA. Would also establish a 'Maryland Data Privacy Implementation and Innovation Workgroup' to study Maryland's consumer data privacy framework across five key areas including data minimization, business compliance challenges, other states' privacy law updates, enforcement capacity, and artificial intelligence and privacy. Findings due to the governor by January 1, 2027.

bills.title: Maryland MODPA Geolocation Data Targeted Advertising Amendment
bills.summary: Would amend MODPA to redefine 'process' to exclude deleting personal data or identifying data for deletion or data minimization, and would prohibit controllers from collecting, processing, sharing, or selling precise geolocation data for targeted advertising without consumer consent.

bills.title: New Hampshire Children's Location and Sensitive Data Sale Prohibition
bills.summary: Amendment to New Hampshire's comprehensive privacy law to prohibit a controller from selling 'the location and other sensitive data regarding children.' Similar to an amendment enacted in Oregon last year. Passed committee on February 2.

bills.title: Pennsylvania Comprehensive Privacy Act (Connecticut-style)
bills.summary: Connecticut-style comprehensive privacy bill that previously passed the Pennsylvania House in October. Re-referred to a new committee this week. Includes a narrow definition of biometric data, no right to access, and a definition of sensitive data that includes certain government identifiers and financial data.
bills.status_detail: Previously passed the Pennsylvania House in October 2025. Re-referred to a new committee this week.

bills.title: Rhode Island Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: AADC variant introduced by Sen. Lawson (D) proposing a blend of Maryland AADC-style applicability, DPIAs, data processing prohibitions and enforcement, and a Colorado/Connecticut-style duty of care to minors with an 'actual knowledge or willful disregard' knowledge standard.

bills.title: South Carolina Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: Age-Appropriate Design Code signed into law on February 5, 2026, immediately effective upon signature. Draws upon prior state privacy laws with novel aspects including a unique duty of care requiring covered services to prevent certain harms to minors, robust tools for all users, third party audit requirements with mandatory public reporting, and personal liability for employees.
bills.status_detail: Signed into law February 5, 2026. Went into effect immediately upon signature.

bills.title: South Dakota ASAA Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework introduced by Rep. Soye (R) with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.

bills.title: Utah App Store Accountability Act (Challenged)
bills.summary: Utah's App Store Accountability Act — existing law. The Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA) filed a federal lawsuit challenging its constitutionality on February 5, arguing broad age verification and parental consent requirements unconstitutionally burden protected speech and are not narrowly tailored, and that the Act's age rating requirements infringe on First Amendment rights and excessively burden interstate commerce.
bills.status_detail: CCIA filed federal lawsuit challenging constitutionality on February 5, 2026.

bills.title: Utah ASAA Family Account Application Exception
bills.summary: Would amend Utah's App Store Accountability Act to provide certain exceptions for developers of 'family account applications' (defined as apps that allow accounts with multiple user profiles and verify that primary account holders are over the age of 18), including not having to verify through the app store's data sharing methods whether verifiable parental consent has been obtained for minor accounts.

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Precise Geolocation Data Sale Prohibition
bills.summary: Would amend the VCDPA to prohibit a controller from selling precise geolocation data. Virginia Senate passed 39-0 on February 3.
bills.status_detail: Virginia Senate passed SB 338 by a vote of 39-0 on February 3, 2026.

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Reproductive and Sexual Health Information Amendment
bills.summary: Proposed amendment to the VCDPA that would add a GLBA data-level exception to the consent requirement for obtaining, disclosing, selling, or disseminating personally identifiable reproductive or sexual health information. Senate voted 39-0 to pass the bill.
bills.status_detail: Senate voted 39-0 to pass the bill.

bills.title: Virginia Verifiable Parental Consent for Minor Registration
bills.summary: Would require verifiable parental consent (VPC) for registering users under the age of 18. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Minor Protections and Duty of Care
bills.summary: Proposed VCDPA amendment concerning minors. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Data-Driven Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: VCDPA amendment to prohibit data-driven pricing. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: Virginia Data Broker Registry
bills.summary: Data broker registry bill. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: Virginia VCDPA Biometrics and Neural Data Amendment
bills.summary: VCDPA amendment concerning biometrics and neural data. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: Virginia Social Media Private Right of Action
bills.summary: Social media private right of action bill. Failed to advance or was held for 2027.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance or held for 2027.

bills.title: West Virginia Comprehensive Privacy Act (CCPA-style)
bills.summary: CCPA-style comprehensive privacy bill introduced by Del. Young (D) that includes a right to correct inaccurate personal information.

bills.title: Wisconsin ASAA Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework introduced by Rep. Goeben (R) on January 29, with divergences including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions. Heard in the Committee on Children and Families on February 5.
bills.status_detail: Heard in the Committee on Children and Families on February 5, 2026.

bills.title: Wisconsin Comprehensive Privacy Act (Connecticut-style)
bills.summary: Connecticut-style comprehensive privacy bill continuing to progress through the Wisconsin Legislature. Has now been re-referred to the Committee on Rules.
bills.status_detail: Re-referred to the Committee on Rules.
